record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a complete metric space, and let T: X -> C(X) be a multivalued mapping such that each value T(x) is closed and, for all x, y in X, the Hausdorff distance H(Tx, Ty) satisfies H(Tx, Ty) < phi(d(x, y)), where phi: [0, +infinity) -> [0, +infinity) is an L-function in the sense that phi(0) = 0, phi(s) > 0 for every s > 0, and for every s > 0 there exists delta > 0 such that phi(t) <= s for all t in a right-neighborhood [delta, delta + epsilon]. Must T have a fixed point, meaning a point x in X such that x belongs to T(x)?

evidence.quote: A point v in X is a fixed point of a map T if v = Tv (when T : X -> X is a single-valued map) or v in Tv (when T : X -> CB(X) is a multi-valued map).

Definition 2.1. [10, 11] Function phi from [0, +infinity) into itself is called an L-function if phi(0) = 0, phi(s) > 0 for all s in (0, +infinity), and for every s in (0, +infinity) there exists delta > 0 such that phi(t) <= s, for all t in [delta, delta + epsilon].

Open Problem 1. Let (X, d) be a complete metric space and T : X -> C(X) a multi-valued mapping such that Tx is closed for every x and H(Tx, Ty) < phi(d(x, y)), for all x, y in X, where phi is an L-function. Does T have a fixed point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a complete metric space, and let $C(X)$ denote the collection of nonempty closed subsets of $X$. The Hausdorff distance on $C(X)$ is
$$H(A,B)=\max\Big\{\sup_{a\in A}\inf_{b\in B}d(a,b),\ \sup_{b\in B}\inf_{a\in A}d(a,b)\Big\}.$$
A function $\varphi:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)$ is called an L-function if $\varphi(0)=0$, $\varphi(s)>0$ for all $s>0$, and for every $s>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\varphi(t)\le s$ for all $t\in[\delta,\delta+\varepsilon]$.

Let $T:X\to C(X)$ be a multivalued mapping (with $T(x)$ nonempty and closed for every $x\in X$) such that there exists an L-function $\varphi$ with
$$H(Tx,Ty)<\varphi(d(x,y))\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in X\text{ with }x\ne y.$$
Question: must $T$ admit a fixed point, i.e., a point $x\in X$ with $x\in T(x)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of this fixed-point existence question for multivalued mappings contracting strictly under an L-function. The problem appears in the multivalued generalization of Lim's contractive condition; standard references on multivalued contractions (Nadler, Lim, Reich, Mizoguchi–Takahashi) and recent work on generalized Hausdorff/controlled metric variants do not report a full solution. Status remains unverified from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Multi-valued contraction mappings (Nadler)
status_evidence.snippet: Nadler's classical extension of Banach's contraction principle to set-valued mappings using Hausdorff distance.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational theorem from which the L-function variant is a strict-inequality generalization; no resolution of the L-function case is given here.

status_evidence.title: On H+ Type Multivalued Contractions and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on multivalued contractions using generalized Hausdorff-type conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Contemporary literature continues to study related contractive conditions without a stated resolution of the strict L-function fixed-point problem.
